purpose: Raise each existing Icon World to a selection-worthy craft level without changing its constitution, adding worlds, hybridizing geometry, expanding the family, or creating app icons.

registrationNodeBudget.rule: A registration node may exist only when removing it changes semantic meaning. Nodes are permitted vocabulary, not mandatory family decoration.

conventionalControlFirewall.rule: Brand grammar must not reduce immediate recognition. Family relationship should come from proportion, stroke, terminal treatment, radius, angle, and bounding-box rhythm rather than semantic lineage machinery.

opticalWeight.principle: Icons should feel equally present rather than mathematically equally sized.

requirements: Authority reads as advice-to-consequence boundary before it reads as connection/crosshair.
Verification moves away from generic square-plus-check confirmation.
Project Memory gains a fundamentally different primary silhouette from Projects.
Provenance becomes a traceability symbol rather than tiny topology notation.
Council and Decision remain related but separate at silhouette level; Decision has a more final destination.
Search loses provenance interruption/node embellishment and preserves conventional magnifier recognition.
Separate Council and Decision without losing editorial quietness.
Move Provenance away from generic activity/signal waveform semantics.
Move Verification away from generic success confirmation.
Preserve density restraint and human optical calm.
Council and Decision must no longer resolve through effectively the same fork/arrow silhouette.
Authority must read as permission boundary rather than directed action.
Supersede must express retained old state plus replacement rather than generic directional action.
Provenance must remain meaningful at 14-16px instead of collapsing into a small line.
quiver-construct.viabilityQuestion: Can Quiver carry AI Council's semantic range without relying predominantly on fork, arrow, and direction motifs?

similarityWarnings.rule: High raster similarity is a human-inspection warning only; low similarity is not evidence of semantic quality.
